crm_notes: Key problem: customers complain when code assistant changes are unpredictable after model updates — reproducibility + pinned model versions is high priority.
Use-case: IDE copilot inside Ember Studio (VSCode + custom remote workspace). Need sub-50ms token streaming to avoid editing lag for remote devs.
Requested features: model/version pinning per workspace, canary rollouts by user cohort, rollback-on-regression, eval gates tied to golden prompt suites.
Acceptance tests: run 1k golden prompts (repo-specific) before promoting new model; zero-regression on top-5 completion diffs and unit test pass rates.
Quote from CTO Priya: 'We need repeatable completions for CI — when engineer runs the same prompt in a test harness, we must get the same output or fail fast.'

Technical asks: ability to pin weights+quant config, snapshot model hash in audit logs, seed control or deterministic sampling, token-level latency SLA, fast fallback to smaller quantized model during capacity pressure.
Routing: prefer regional routing (NA) and fall back to lower-cost variant for non-critical suggestions. Need explicit cost telemetry per-prompt.
POC scope: 2-week canary; measure reproducibility (hash stability), latency p50/p95, token-cost delta vs baseline, and developer acceptance scores.
Eval gates discussed: automated eval pipeline (on PR) that runs golden prompts, compares diffs, and blocks rollout if regressions > threshold; want Redwood Optimize hooks.
SE notes: suggest using prefix/KV caching for large workspace context to reduce token cost and maintain low latency on repeated completions.
Legal: data residency for EU customers; Ember wants option to run Private for enterprise customers with retention controls.
Next technical deliverable: Redwood to provide canary config YAML, example eval harness, and deterministic seeding doc by 2026-03-17.
summary: EmberCode Labs is evaluating Redwood to power an IDE copilot and code completion product. Primary requirements are model/version pinning for reproducibility, canary rollouts with eval gates, deterministic seeding for CI tests, low-latency streaming in remote IDEs, and enterprise-grade security (VPC/KMS/audit logs). POC planned to validate canary + eval gate workflow and latency/cost tradeoffs.
